style.name: Endless Zoom
style.description: One continuous, constant-speed zoom inward through nested worlds, each a bright toy-like 3D relief in its own clean colour key (cream chat app, coral token tiles, electric-blue glowing value sliders, golden neural network, green circuit board with a chip, violet switch with a spark). Every world is authored at unit size around a portal at its centre whose face is the next world's colour; the camera dollies in exponentially (one rate for the whole loop, so perceived speed never changes), the next world fades in on the portal's face and grows until it fills the frame, and only two worlds are ever drawn (the outer one directly, the inner one rendered through the portal as a live window). The last portal contains the first world: the loop closes and the final frame equals the first. A rising Shepard scale and a chime per crossing come from the same zoom clock.
motion: The zoom is s(t) = exp(k t) with one k for the whole loop: constant perceived speed, scale computed from t, never accumulated.
Only two worlds are drawn: the outer one directly, the inner one rendered to a target and shown through the portal window.
The inner world fades in on the portal's face (whose colour is its background), then grows until it is the frame.
Inside each world, small motion (bobbing tiles, settling sliders, travelling pulses, flickering switches) runs on the world's own local clock, so a world looks the same on every visit.
The camera only sways (periodic yaw/pitch of a few degrees) for parallax; the dolly itself is the zoom.

notes.mechanism: zoom.js: S_m(t) = exp(k (tau - tau_m)), tau = t + phase wrapped; k = ln(prod R) / duration; T_m = ln R_m / k. Two worlds drawn per frame: the outer one directly, the inner one through the portal window (render target, SDF mask, alpha from S_inner).
